newsitem.title: USA: Clinton selects Asian-American for top Justice job.
newsitem.headline: Clinton selects Asian-American for top Justice job.

text.p: President Bill Clinton will name California lawyer Bill Lann Lee to be assistant attorney general for civil rights, making him the first Asian-American to hold that post, the White House said on Thursday.
Lee, 48, the son of immigrants, is director of the western regional office of the Legal Defence and Educational Fund of the National Association for the Advancement of Coloured People (NAACP).

"As a litigator, Mr. Lee is known as a pragmatic attorney and skilled coalition builder. For the past 23 years, he has worked with a wide variety of organisations and citizens in order to achieve consensus and obtain justice for victims of discrimination," a White House statement said.

Word of Lee's nomination came as Clinton prepared for a major speech on U.S. race relations. White House spokesman Mike McCurry said that later on Thursday Clinton would make public the names of those who will serve on a new blue-ribbon panel that is to examine the delicate social issue.

Clinton, who wants to be remembered as a president who worked for racial and ethnic harmony in the United States, was scheduled to discuss the subject in a commencement speech at the University of California at San Diego on Saturday.

Lee, regarded in legal circles as one of the nation's top civil rights lawyers, has helped lead a court challenge to a California referendum vote to ban affirmative action, the system of preferences to correct past race and gender bias.
As a result, his nomination could face opposition in the Senate from conservative Republicans who oppose affirmative action. Lee would require Senate confirmation.
The White House said Clinton also intended to nominate Raymond Fisher, another California lawyer, to be associate attorney general. That is the third highest post in the Justice Department.
Fisher, 57, was a private attorney who specialised in business and civil cases. He was perhaps best known as head of the Los Angeles Police Commission.
